sector_selloff.description: Three chip names fall together -- one story, not three.

judge verdict.failure: The brief asserts causation in the opening sentence with 'the widening of chip export rules, with all three semiconductor names down sharply' and 'The one story driving your watchlist', both presenting the export rules as definitively causing the moves rather than using correlational framing.

sector_selloff.first_output:
The one story driving your watchlist is the widening of chip export rules, with all three semiconductor names down sharply. MU took the worst of it at -7.2%, which may be related to reports that memory rules tightened specifically. NVDA fell 6.1% and AMD 5.4%, both moving alongside the broader semiconductor selloff. KO was flat at +0.2%.

The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.2%, twice the S&P's -0.4% decline, reflecting the weight of chip stocks in the tech-heavy index. Market headlines note this was the semiconductor index's worst session since March.

None of the names you're tracking reports earnings in the next week -- all four have dates set for 30 days out.
